questions.prompt: Directions: Suppose the university newspaper is inviting submissions from the students for its coming edition on the recent development in their hometown.You are now to write an essay for submission. You will have 30 minutes to write the essay. You should write at least 120 words but no more than 180 words.
questions.correctAnswer:
My hometown has changed noticeably in recent years, especially in the way public spaces serve local residents. A former unused riverside area has become a pleasant walking route with benches, trees and spaces for community activities.

In the past, families had few convenient places to spend time outdoors. Now, older people can meet friends along the river, children have a safe area to play and students can take a quiet walk after school. Improved bus connections also make the area easier to reach. These changes may appear ordinary, but they affect daily life more directly than a single impressive building.

I am glad to see development that pays attention to residents' practical needs. At the same time, public facilities require maintenance and responsible use. By keeping these spaces clean and listening to feedback, my hometown can continue improving while preserving the friendly relationships that make it feel like home.

questions.hint: 围绕家乡最近一项具体发展展开，并比较过去和现在。
questions.explanation:
以下为按题意独立写成的参考范文，作文没有唯一答案。河边公共空间与交通改善展示日常变化；结尾写维护和居民需求，不需虚构经济数据。示例可换为自己的家乡事实。

先指出家乡近期公共空间与交通发展，再用河边空间、出行改善说明对居民的影响，结尾写维护及持续需求。public spaces是公共空间，local residents是当地居民，improve daily life是改善生活。recent development要求变化而非静态城市介绍；现在完成时适合强调近年成果。写地点与对生活的影响即可，不必凭空给GDP或人口数字。若用个人家乡经历，可把示范场景换成实际变化。

练习方法：先用提示列三段提纲，在30分钟内独立写作，再按下方标准逐项打分；把失分最多的一段重写。参考范文约149词（缩写、连字符词按一词，含标题或书信称呼落款），满足120–180词要求；评分用于练习自检，不代表官方阅卷分数。
rubric: 练习自评总分15分：题目覆盖0–6＋结构0–4＋语言0–5，先独立写完再对照；观点不同于范文也可得满分，只要有合理支持。
题目覆盖0–6分：该题检查——围绕家乡最近一项具体发展展开，并比较过去和现在。。6分=任务完整且有具体理由/活动/例证；4–5分=切题但细节偏薄；2–3分=遗漏主要任务；0–1分=基本离题。
结构0–4分：4分=开头明确任务、主体按逻辑展开、结尾回扣，段间自然；3分=顺序清楚但局部衔接生硬；1–2分=跳跃或机械罗列；0分=内容难以组织理解。
语言0–5分：5分=语法和用词基本准确、句型有变化；3–4分=少量错误但不影响理解；1–2分=反复出现时态、主谓一致或搭配错误并影响阅读；0分=多数句子不能理解。
格式与修订：按原题保持120–180词；新闻/书信/提案用对应体裁，明确要求的首句逐字保留。若超限、少写任务或缺必要格式，先修改再评分，不把字数达标当作内容满分。

So Ciara Kelly and colleagues recruited 129 hobbyists to look at how the time spent on their hobbies [27] ____ their work life.

The researchers found that when participants spent longer than [28] ____ on their leisure activity, their belief in their ability to perform their job was strengthened. But this was only the [29] ____ when they had a serious hobby that was dissimilar to their job, or when their hobby was similar to their work but they only did it [30] ____ . When their hobby was both serious and similar to their job, then spending more time on it actually decreased their work [31] ____ .

Why might that be? To maintain a serious hobby, people need to invest significant psychological resources, say the authors—so if the activity has the same kinds of demands as their work, they may be left [32] ____ and unable to perform well at their job. But if their hobby is quite different from their career, it may not [33] ____ in the same way but instead help them develop other knowledge and skills that can [34] ____ their confidence at work. "Consider a scientist who is a keen rock climber," says Kelly. "Since climbing is so far [35] ____ from their day-to-day work activities, they can still recover from the demands of their job with plenty of resources."

questions.prompt: In the absence of Federal legislation, some states in the US have passed laws concerning paid family leave.
questions.passage:
More fathers are taking paternity leave, but mothers are still doing all the work

A) Attitudes towards paternity leave(陪产假) have drastically changed in America in the last five years as more fathers feel comfortable taking extended time off, but gender bias persists when it comes to career prospects and the home, according to a new study of working parents.

B) Research by the Boston College Center for Work & Family, which surveyed new parents at four large US companies who were qualified for taking at least six weeks paid parental leave, found that 81% of the 1,240 employees surveyed said the notion of fathers taking leave has become more acceptable.

C) Of those surveyed, 62% of fathers took the maximum amount of time off compared to 93% of mothers, and around three-quarters of workers said their employer was equally supportive of mothers and fathers taking parental leave and over half said leave policies had made workplace culture better.

D) The US is one of only three countries in the world not to offer statutory(法定的) paid leave, but increasingly states and companies are starting to take up the issue. So far, eight states and the District of Columbia have their own paid family leave laws.

E) Brad Harrington, executive director of the center and lead author of the study, estimates only 20% to 30% of companies in the US offer paid parental leave. He feels the research findings reflect an obvious change in corporate attitudes to new fathers taking time off.

F) "We did a study on paternity leave five years ago. Compared with those findings, these numbers were shocking to me. I did not expect 80% of people to say the organisation finds dads taking this leave acceptable and three-quarters to say it's equally supportive of women and men taking leave," Harrington said.

G) The previous study found that nearly three-quarters of fathers saw two to four weeks as an appropriate duration for paternity leave and 76% said they would prefer not to take all their time off at once.

H) Since then, there have been a number of legal cases against companies involving paternity leave—including cases against JPMorgan Chase and Estee Lauder—which have helped put pressure on companies to make their parental leave policies gender neutral.

I) However, the study also shows how traditional gender roles endure both at work, where more women than men reported changes in their perceived career potential, and at home—even among workers who claim to have a strong desire for equality.

questions.prompt: What does a "multitasker" originally refer to?
questions.passage:
A multitasker is one who can perform two or more tasks effectively at the same time, which—apart from the obvious differences—is similar to what a computer does. The concept does indeed come from the realms of technology, where it is used to refer to an operating system that can execute multiple tasks at the same time. However, the question is: can a person really be a multitasker?

For most scientists, the answer is no. So much so that, according to experts in neuroscience(神经系统科学), our brains do not handle multitasking situations well. As soon as two tasks require our attention, productivity suffers. What we call multitasking, therefore, is in reality the ability to move more or less quickly from one task to another. This requires two essential conditions: that one of the tasks needs to be automatic, like walking or eating, and that they both need different mental processes. Answering the phone and writing at the same time, for example.

However, on the other side of the coin there are people who maintain that it is possible to be, or at least seem to be, multitasking. A recent study concluded that regardless of whether people are actually handling several tasks or not, the mere fact that they perceive this activity as multitasking has a positive effect on their performance.

The business perspective offers a different view: multitasking is understood as the ability to adapt to all types of environment within a company and effectively undertake different activities within a set time frame. Indeed, many companies look for people who are skilled in multitasking to improve their productivity. From this different perspective, you can not only be multitasking but this ability can also be taught: something that is easier in fluid organisations, which favour flexibility in their working practices.

The benefits of multitasking are clear. Being quicker and more efficient increases our performance and the number of tasks completed. But having to pay attention to several things at once means that the powers of concentration are reduced and that can lead to more mistakes.

A skilled worker executing more than one task at the same time.

An efficient person able to perform multiple tasks at the same time.
